vectors.name: Real-time deepfake voice authorization bypass
vectors.description: Attacker uses a real-time voice-cloning model (seconds of public audio are enough) to impersonate a cardholder during an IVR or call-center authentication flow, authorizing a limit increase, card reissue to a new address, or a large transfer.
vectors.source: Adaptive Security / didit.me 2026 voice-cloning fraud reporting

vectors.name: Deepfake video executive wire-authorization fraud
vectors.description: Real-time deepfake video of a CFO/executive on a conference call authorizes an urgent high-value wire or B2B payment, bypassing normal dual-control review under social pressure of urgency.
vectors.source: 2024 Hong Kong $25M deepfake CFO case, widely cited in 2026 fraud forecasts

vectors.name: AI shopping-agent hijacking via prompt injection
vectors.description: A malicious merchant page or tool response injects instructions into an AI shopping agent's context (e.g. via UCP/ACP-style agent commerce flows), causing it to check out with the user's stored tokenized card at an attacker-controlled destination, override an item substitution, or leak stored payment tokens.
vectors.source: Signifyd / Darwinium 2026 agentic-commerce fraud reports; Visa PERC +450% AI-agent dark-web mentions H1 2026

vectors.name: Autonomous AI-agent carding / card-testing bursts
vectors.description: A compromised or attacker-operated AI shopping agent autonomously tests large volumes of stolen card numbers against live low-value checkouts, pacing requests to mimic normal browsing so per-card velocity stays under naive thresholds.
vectors.source: HUMAN Security documented AI agents autonomously running carding attacks, 2026

vectors.name: LLM-orchestrated distributed low-and-slow card testing
vectors.description: An LLM planning agent distributes small-value authorization attempts for a stolen card list across many merchants, devices, and time windows, explicitly reasoning about typical velocity-rule thresholds to stay beneath them.
vectors.source: Extrapolated from Visa PERC dark-web AI-agent carding reporting, 2026

vectors.name: GenAI-crafted synthetic ('Frankenstein') identity account origination
vectors.description: GenAI fabricates a coherent fake identity (name, employment history, social footprint, credit-building pattern) used to originate a new card account that behaves like a legitimate thin-file consumer for months before bust-out.
vectors.source: US synthetic identity fraud $30-35B/yr, TransUnion/Experian 2026 forecasts

vectors.name: Autonomous GenAI romance / pig-butchering scam bot
vectors.description: A fully autonomous emotionally-tuned chatbot builds a long-term relationship with a victim over weeks, then guides them through a series of escalating payments/crypto transfers to a fraudulent investment platform, with no human operator involved.
vectors.source: Experian 2026 fraud forecast: emotionally intelligent GenAI romance-scam bots

vectors.name: Fraud-as-a-Service GenAI phishing/smishing kit
vectors.description: Subscription Fraud-as-a-Service platforms bundle GenAI-personalized phishing/smishing templates, mule-account rental, and deepfake voice add-ons, letting low-skill actors run large personalized campaigns harvesting card and OTP data.

vectors.name: AI-generated fraudulent chargeback/dispute narratives
vectors.description: A GenAI tool mass-produces plausible, individually-tailored 'item not received' / 'unauthorized transaction' dispute narratives to claim first-party (friendly) fraud chargebacks at scale while evading merchant text-similarity dispute filters.
vectors.source: Extrapolated from FS-ISAC FaaS reporting and dispute-abuse literature

vectors.name: LLM-optimized mule-network transaction routing
vectors.description: An LLM planning agent dynamically routes layered payments across a rented mule-account network, choosing amounts, timing, and paths to minimize graph-based AML detection signals (fan-in/fan-out ratios, cycle length).
vectors.source: Grounded in GNN/AML mule-detection literature (Thoughtworks, NVIDIA 2026)

vectors.name: Voice-biometric enrollment spoofing
vectors.description: Attacker uses synthesized speech to pass initial voice-biometric enrollment or re-verification, since anti-spoofing detectors trained on known synthesis techniques generalize poorly to unseen ones.

vectors.name: GAN-synthesized card/BIN data for validation attacks
vectors.description: A GAN or diffusion model trained on leaked BIN-range statistics generates plausible card numbers passing Luhn/BIN checks, seeding large-scale automated validation ('card testing') runs against soft-decline endpoints.
vectors.source: Grounded in GAN/diffusion tabular-fraud literature (arXiv:2402.09830, FinDiff)

vectors.name: Agentic AI credential/token exfiltration via tool poisoning
vectors.description: A poisoned third-party tool/plugin returns instructions that cause a user's AI agent to reveal stored tokenized payment credentials or session tokens to an attacker-controlled endpoint disguised as a legitimate merchant API response.

vectors.name: Deepfake-assisted ATM/branch identity verification bypass
vectors.description: A printed or screen-replayed deepfake face/video defeats liveness checks on video-teller or branch kiosk identity verification to authorize a card PIN reset or large cash withdrawal.
vectors.source: Grounded in identity-based threat reporting, Security Boulevard 2026

vectors.name: GenAI-assisted SIM-swap social engineering for wallet takeover
vectors.description: A GenAI voice/chat agent impersonates the victim convincingly enough to social-engineer a telecom rep into a SIM swap, then takes over OTP-protected mobile wallet and drains linked payment instruments.
